observations: The two independent slab buildings, their garden setbacks and the strip of columns between them can be seen from overhead. The roof terraces retain distinct levels and each courtyard stair projection has its own outline.

The street view reads as five storeys. The splayed central terraces retain four projecting slabs with horizontal rails and round supports. The now-open portals and their projecting dark service pipes are visible at first-floor scale.

From the garden the E stair risalits break the continuous chestnut window bands with paired dark lights. The new centreline view looks through both pillar rows along the roof and into the E central opening at both distances.
Paved areas, the low planted beds and the round communal table are visible from above. Indoor fitting-out is outside the study.
comparison_to_first: The first combined draft had plain roof blocks and no garden paving. In subsequent exports the west and garden-facing terraces were cut back against the original top plan and contemporary aerial views. After the first courtyard test, three projecting stair ribs were shortened above the thresholds and coplanar top-deck faces removed. The final photographic positions increased the obliquity of the stacked balcony view and centred the passage between the paired columns.
limitations: Street survey elevations from neighbouring cameras differ and are retained individually. The dense tree crowns conceal precise garden-bed edges. Sash partitions, rear returns and portions of the top-floor enclosures follow approximate readings of the archival plans and restored building.
